newsitem.title: USA: Marvel gets bondholder plan for infusion.
newsitem.headline: Marvel gets bondholder plan for infusion.

text.p: Marvel Entertainment Group Inc. said Friday its bondholders have proposed a $365 million infusion for the company as part of a plan that may allow it to emerge from Chapter 11 bankruptcy.

The bondholders, led by investor Carl Icahn, went to court last month to fight an alternative reorganization plan proposed by financier Ronald Perelman's Andrews Group for the publisher of Spiderman, X-Men and the Incredible Hulk comics.
As a result of the new proposal, Andrews terminated its agreement to buy stock in a reorganized Marvel, the New York-based company said.

Under the bondholders' proposal, the $365 million would be funded by owners of Marvel equity, including bondholders, through a rights offering that would be backed by entities controlled by Icahn, Marvel said.
Unlike Andrews' proposal, this plan does not involve Toy Biz Inc. becoming a Marvel unit.

Marvel said it has authorised management to work with the bondholders to conduct their due diligence and develop definite documentation. The due diligence is expected to be completed by March 21, it added.
Andrews in December said it had tentatively agreed to acquire all class A shares of Toy Biz stock held by Toy Biz public stockholders for $22.50 per share as part of a plan to reorganize Marvel.
Marvel's stock edged up 12.5 cents to $2.50 early on the New York Stock Exchange.
